### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 37 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f7d740376d3953c7b4a7d22c77e0f689c77a228a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6a5ad5e46cb82d847f2d943705b34defbc5d2637` — the merge of head `970f966b9fc2d49f623ec2ab511ac62012bd458b` into base `f7d740376d3953c7b4a7d22c77e0f689c77a228a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6a5ad5e46cb82d847f2d943705b34defbc5d2637 && git checkout 6a5ad5e46cb82d847f2d943705b34defbc5d2637
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f7d740376d3953c7b4a7d22c77e0f689c77a228a 970f966b9fc2d49f623ec2ab511ac62012bd458b && git checkout -B drift-repro f7d740376d3953c7b4a7d22c77e0f689c77a228a && git merge --no-ff 970f966b9fc2d49f623ec2ab511ac62012bd458b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f7d740376d3953c7b4a7d22c77e0f689c77a228a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `970f966b9f`
Local-runs: none

Scope: the net diff against the merge base (4 files, +163/−0):
- `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts`: the local `CEREMONY_OWNED_DROP_COLUMN`, `isCeremonyOwnedColumnDrop()` and `ceremonyOwnedDropFinding()`;
- `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts`: the boot reconcile's warning loop asks `isTenantKeyCertified()` once per table, only for an `organization_id` `drop_column` about to be warned;
- the new `sql-driver.ceremony-owned-drop-line.test.ts`;
- the changeset.

Read with them:
- the card #24956, seat 2's serial note 6303725599, the claim 6333744317 and the dispatch 6333771718;
- the dev's `os-dev-report` 6335859221, read as claims;
- the PR body;
- `schema-drift.ts`'s `DESTRUCTIVE_COLUMN_REMEDY` and `driftFindingWithoutRemedy`;
- `SqlDriver.isTenantKeyCertified()` / `setTenantKeyCertifiedResolver()` (PR #24893);
- the CLI's `apply-drop-gates.ts` `organization_id` entry and footer (PR #24954) and `organization-ownership-drop-gate.ts`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **One source decides, as the card asks: right.**
  - **The source.** The line is changed only when `isTenantKeyCertified()` answers no. That is the driver's own reader over the engine-handed `isOrganizationOwnershipCertified()`. There is no second list and no copy of the CLI gate.
  - **The constant.** `CEREMONY_OWNED_DROP_COLUMN` names a column, not a table set. `driver-sql` cannot import the CLI's `ORGANIZATION_COLUMN`, so a local constant is the honest spelling.
- **This card's population answers no.** The dev measured on a real `create-objectstack@17.7.0` SQLite database (43 tables carry `organization_id`).
  - **Before the fix.** `os serve` and `os migrate apply --yes` each print 28 `[schema-drift]` lines, 9 of them `organization_id` drops naming `--allow-destructive`. `apply --allow-destructive` is refused.
  - **After the fix.** The same 9 name the ceremony, and the other 19 lines diff empty against `main`.
  - **No fork.** The boot's own `recreate_index` lines on that database already say "This database is not certified", so the fork the claim named did not occur.
- **The text is the finding plus the plan's wording.** `driftFindingWithoutRemedy` removes exactly the `drop_column` remedy sentence. Then the line takes the entry wording `os migrate plan` uses (`apply-drop-gates.ts`, "a drop the organization-ownership ceremony owns, and it has not verified on this database").
  - **The ending.** The boot line ends with `run "os migrate organization-ownership", which drops it itself.`, where the plan says "(see below)" and points at its footer. The boot has no footer, so naming the command is the right ending.
- **Nothing else moves.** The new branch is a `continue` before the existing `warn`. What the boot applies, what it skips and `driftWarned`'s de-duplication are unchanged.
  - **One ask per table.** The question is asked lazily, `certified ??= await …`, once per call, so once per table, and only when such a drop is about to be warned.
  - **A yes is kept.** The reader keeps a yes, and a no is asked again on the next table.
- **The pins have teeth.** Six cases on real SQLite:
  - not certified: names the ceremony, never `--allow-destructive`, and the reader is asked once;
  - no resolver handed over: the same line;
  - certified: the differ's message byte for byte;
  - two not-certified controls, an orphan `legacy_code` drop and a `tighten_not_null`, unchanged;
  - a table with no such drop never asks.

  **Ablation.** With the guard prefixed `false &&`, pins 1 and 2 go red and 3 to 6 stay green; restored blob-equal to `HEAD`.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` for `@objectstack/driver-sql`: right for a log line's remedy text. No response, status, error, outcome or export of the public entry moves. `isCeremonyOwnedColumnDrop` / `ceremonyOwnedDropFinding` are exported from `schema-drift.ts` but are not in `src/index.ts`'s named re-export list from it (which carries `driftFindingWithoutRemedy`), so the published surface does not widen.
- The changeset and the PR body carry the claim's `Clause-②: no (operator log line text only)` verbatim at a line start, and `Metadata-protocol: none`. `none` is right, since nothing a metadata author writes changes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Cross-lane:** none. All four files are `driver-sql`'s. The CLI drop gate and `apply-drop-gates.ts` are read, not edited. `@objectstack/cli` passed its unit (4769) and integration (1447) layers against the change.
- **Not governed:** `check-governed-merges` matched 0 of 4 paths, and the PR has 163 changed lines. `git merge-tree --write-tree` against today's `origin/main` is clean.
- **The 18.0-born case stays outside.** A database born on 18.0 (birth marker, so certified) whose object newly drops `organization_id` still prints `--allow-destructive`, which the CLI gate refuses. That is #24638's population (`domain:cli`, `pm:blocked`), as the claim fenced it.
- **The dev's observation, noted and not filed.** Orphaned indexes keyed on `organization_id` (`drop_index`) still name `--allow-destructive` on a pre-ceremony database, at boot and in `os migrate plan`. The CLI gate judges `drop_column` only, and a run that carries those index drops on such a database also carries the column drops it refuses. Whether an index drop is held is the gate's question. It sits in the PR's Acceptance notes.
- **Deviations, all accepted:**
  - the base moved (`82cfaf792`, then the merge of `6251f5905`);
  - 28 lines today, not the card's 22, with all 9 `organization_id` drops covered;
  - the measurement setup (`engines.protocol` bumped on the scaffold, not on the database);
  - the CLI integration layer run as well;
  - the AGENTS.md commit trailers.
- **Open questions:** both are answered **A** by the seat: name the ceremony rather than print no remedy, and a local constant. They sit inside the claim's fence.
- **Docs:** the dev found no `content/docs/**` page that quotes the boot line. `deployment/cli.mdx`'s drift table stays true.
- **CI on `970f966b9f`:** 2 of 40 check-runs still running at this read. The ACCEPT waits for green.
